description: Original, fictional DayMaker editorial asides. Not advertiser sponsorship claims.

lines.text: Our weather-control machine is still a desk fan.
We priced a private satellite. We now own binoculars.
Our cloud-removal department is one person waving a towel.
The office umbrella is technically a colander.
We requested central air. The sun declined.
The company yacht is a leaf in a puddle.
Our storm-chasing vehicle is a folding chair.
Our rain machine has been downgraded to a spray bottle.
Our weather-control budget bought half a desk fan.
We cannot expense an emotional-support snowplow. Apparently.
Karen: I asked for a company jet. They gave me a weather balloon.
Karen: The executive lounge is a chair that faces the window.
Karen: I requested valet parking. The bicycle rack has yet to respond.
Karen: Our office spa is a humidifier with a handwritten sign.
Karen: My corner office has four corners. Somehow this was the upgrade.
Karen: The break-room espresso machine is a kettle with ambition.
Karen: I filed a complaint about the revolving door. It came back around.
Karen: The dress code says business casual. The office fern is pushing it.
Frat Bro: Our corporate retreat is two lawn chairs and a cooler.
Frat Bro: Team building is stacking coffee cups. Current record: three.
Frat Bro: The office gym is one resistance band and a lot of confidence.
Frat Bro: We have stadium seating. Both stools are incredible.
Frat Bro: Corporate catering just dropped. Somebody brought pretzels.
Frat Bro: The office trophy is a gold-painted stapler. Elite hardware.
Frat Bro: Our VIP rooftop is a very respectable stepladder.
Frat Bro: The team mascot is a sock puppet. Absolute locker-room legend.
Grandpa: The company car is a wheelbarrow. Excellent mileage.
Grandpa: Our paper shredder is a goat on a consulting contract.
Grandpa: The office clock needs winding. Finally, a task with clear instructions.
Grandpa: Our standing desk is a regular desk on four dictionaries.
Grandpa: The company picnic has one rule: return my good blanket.
Grandpa: We upgraded the suggestion box. It now has a lid.
Grandpa: Our office antiques are just things I brought in on Monday.
Grandpa: The company library has three books and my missing glasses.
Politician: The cloud-removal committee has scheduled another meeting.
Politician: We have unanimously approved a larger minutes folder.
Politician: The ribbon-cutting scissors are awaiting their own opening ceremony.
Politician: Our office plant has broad support across the windowsill.
Politician: The snack committee has reached a historic agreement on crackers.
Politician: We are forming a working group to locate the working printer.
Politician: The new podium is a shoebox. Our ambitions remain full size.
Politician: Our five-year office plan begins with finding a pen.
2-Year-Old: Company car go beep. Is cardboard.
2-Year-Old: I made office castle. Nobody move couch pillows.
2-Year-Old: Boss said big ideas. I drew VERY big noodle.
2-Year-Old: Meeting has snacks? I am meeting expert.
2-Year-Old: Office fish got promoted. Has bigger cup.
2-Year-Old: I answer company phone. Is banana. Line busy.
2-Year-Old: Our printer makes pictures. I make printer purple.
2-Year-Old: Company nap room is everywhere if you believe.
